stories.title: 500,000 Chromebooks to be distributed among students across country over 2 years, announces PM Shehbaz
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced on Sunday that the government would distribute 500,000 Chromebook laptops to students nationwide over two years.
He said this at the launch ceremony of the Prime Minister’s Youth Chromebook Scheme in Islamabad.
In August, the premier, speaking on the occasion of International Youth Day, said that 250,000 high-achieving students would be awarded Chromebook laptops this year.

stories.title: Hina Javed murder case: In open letter to Punjab CM, victim's family again expresses mistrust in police probe
summary: Her husband and their domestic worker were arrested as Hina’s family accused them of murdering her while her father-in-law was questioned as part of the investigation.
The family requested CM Maryam to look into the case file in detail and see the evidence linking Hina’s husband “to the murder being ignored from day one”.

Last month, the Punjab government constituted a three-member high-powered committee to review the investigation into the murder, in which Hina’s husband and domestic servant have been sent on judicial remand.

stories.title: Why are Pakistan wearing a pink jersey today?
summary: As part of the initiative, not only is the Pakistan team coloured pink, but members of the English cricket team, match officials and commentators are also wearing pink ribbons for the cause, in order “to demonstrate solidarity with breast cancer patients and survivors”.
South Africa hosts a “Pink Day” One-day International every year at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg, where the home team wears pink kits to raise awareness about breast cancer.
Pakistan hosted a similar pink day last year as well, as part of the T20I series against South Africa.

stories.title: Resumption of war with with Israel, US will not change Iran's positions: Araghchi
summary: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that a potential resumption of war with Israel and the United States would not change his country’s positions.

Iran has claimed control over the strait since the outbreak of the war and has regularly targeted vessels that attempt crossing without its authorisation — moves strongly opposed by Washington and countries in the region.

In June, Iran agreed with the United States to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, laying out a pathway to a permanent settlement of the conflict, only for the deal to later unravel as each side accused the other of violating it.

stories.title: Trump calls Obama ‘grossly incompetent’ after ex-president unloads on him at rallies ahead of US midterms
summary: Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration.

Campaigning in Michigan for El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a “circuit breaker” to “at least rein in some of the foolishness” of Trump’s presidency. “We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government,” Obama said.
Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats.

stories.title: Indian protesters clash with police over dam project bordering China
summary: Indian protesters angry over a proposed Himalayan mega-dam, intended to counter an upstream Chinese hydropower project, have clashed with police and torched buildings, officials said.
India says the proposed dam is needed to counter China’s $167-billion Yaxia project, a likely record-breaking hydropower scheme upstream in Tibet.
India’s proposed dam, which would be by far its largest hydropower project, has drawn fierce opposition from local communities who fear the loss of their homes and land.

stories.title: Shadab returns, Razaullah makes debut as Pakistan elect to field in tri-series match against England
summary: Pakistan won the toss and elected to field against England in the One-day International tri-series match at the Gaddafi Stadium on Sunday, with all-rounder Shadab Khan returning to the side and Razaullah making his debut.
Captain Shaheen Shah Afridi confirmed two changes to the Pakistan side, with Shadab coming in after missing the first two matches of the tri-series.
Teams: Pakistan: Shaheen Shah Afridi (captain), Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan (wicket-keeper), Salman Ali Agha, Hasan Nawaz, Shadab Khan, Abrar Ahmed, Razaullah, Haris Rauf.

stories.title: Trailer runs over, kills two on Karachi's Mai Kolachi Road
summary: KARACHI: A fast-moving trailer ran over and killed a young man and a teenage girl on Mai Kolachi Road on Saturday.
The officer said the victims’ parents told the police that they did not want to pursue any legal proceedings.
In a separate incident, an unidentified young man was killed when an unknown vehicle hit his motorcycle on the National Highway near Quaid-i-Azam Park in Steel Town on Saturday, rescue services said.

stories.title: Four Mpox cases detected in KP
summary: As health experts fear the risk of the local transmission of the virus, the health department has planned contact tracing and testing of the close relatives of the infected people, say officials.

Health officials said the department had already issued guidelines to hospitals, especially those in affected districts, asking them to collect samples from suspected Mpox patients for laboratory confirmation to ensure strict surveillance through timely diagnosis.
They said Mpox cases reported in the province previously were mainly linked to international travel, with patients contracting the infection abroad before entering the country.

stories.title: First infant battling mpox dies in Karachi hospital
summary: KARACHI: An infant boy battling mpox for more than a week at a hospital died early on Saturday morning — the first mortality of a baby from the contagious viral infection in Karachi.
Sources told Dawn that the 52-day-old baby boy had reportedly contracted the infection during circumcision performed at an “illegal” hospital located in Malir.
The sources said nearly all victims were either infants or newborns who contracted the infection from hospital/clinic settings lacking infection control protocols.

stories.title: Rawalpindi Development Authority told to digitise financial management to evade scams
summary: RAWALPINDI: The commissioner has directed the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) to introduce a digital financial management system to avoid financial scams.

During the meeting, the commissioner directed the concerned officials to introduce a digital financial management system to improve transparency, efficiency, accountability, and the overall performance of the authority.
He directed the Finance Wing RDA to adopt modern digital solutions for financial transactions, record management, and official correspondence.

summary: LAHORE: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has arrested a suspect for allegedly threatening minors to sell their private pictures and videos on pornographic websites.
According to the investigation, the suspect contacted minors through social media platforms and obtained their objectionable pictures and videos to blackmail them.

stories.title: Nasirabad pylon blast cuts power to many areas of Sindh, Punjab
summary: DERA MURAD JAMALI: Power supply to several areas of Sindh and Punjab was disrupted from the Uch Power Plant in Nasirabad district after unidentified men blew up a 220kV high-voltage transmission pylon near Dera Murad Jamali, officials said on Saturday.
Nasirabad SSP Asad Khan Nasar stated that an improvised explosive device (IED) was planted under the power pylon in the Goth Mughal Khan Bugti area in the early hours of Saturday.

The powerful blast destroyed the pylon, suspending the power supply to several cities, including Shikarpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Sadiqabad, Sukkur, Larkana, Jacobabad, Kashmore, and Guddu, as well as some areas in Dera Murad Jamali.

stories.title: Infantino laughs off resignation talk
summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning in the wake of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, pointing to overwhelming support from member associations around the globe.

His prospects for reelection strengthened on Friday after the head of Asian football endorsed him for a fourth term, with Asian Football confederation (AFC) President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa saying Asia was united behind Infantino.

I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view," Infantino told the BBC as he laughed off a question about whether he had considered stepping down.

stories.title: Decoding defence deals
summary: These defence deals have, in the past year, increased Pakistan’s strategic relevance in the Middle East.
There are four primary strategic factors that have driven Islamabad’s emphasis on the joint defence production clause in each defence pact.

By integrating affluent Saudi and Qatari capital with the technologically advanced Turkish weapons industry, Pakistan is building an insulated, collaborative defence network with the middle powers to achieve this strategic objective.

stories.title: Japan's Yoshida wins first LPGA Tour title
summary: Japan's Yuri Yoshida captured her first LPGA Tour title on Sunday with a nervy one-shot victory at the Ladies Championship in South Korea.
Perhaps sensing a maiden LPGA victory, Yoshida stumbled with a bogey at the 15th, birdied the 17th and then bogeyed the final hole.
But with overnight leader Ryu Hae-ran also dropping a shot at the 18th, Yoshida's final-round four-under-par 68 was enough to get the job done.

stories.title: Bestway launches Geely Auto in Pakistan
summary: ISLAMABAD: Bestway Group on Saturday launched Chinese automaker Geely Auto in Pakistan, acquiring the Proton plant at Port Qasim, Karachi, for assembly.
Bestway said it has invested over $350 million in Pakistan and created 20,000 jobs in the last three years.
Geely Auto Inter­national Corporation Vice President Evin Ye said Pakistan was Geely’s first market in South Asia, adding that it was the only automaker with a low-orbit satellite network.

stories.title: Pakistan's trade gap with Gulf partners narrows
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s trade deficit with Gulf partner countries narrowed 26.35 per cent to $2.85bn in the first quarter of 2026-27 against $3.87bn a year earlier, largely due to lower imports and moderately higher exports.
On the export side, the UAE accounted for approximately 66.21pc of Pakistan’s total exports to the seven countries in 1QFY27, followed by Saudi Arabia at 19.45pc.
Exports to Qatar fell by nearly 22.79pc, while imports dipped by 72.51pc in 1QFY27 year on year.

stories.title: Prudent warning
summary: AS speculation grows regarding fresh US-Israeli aggression against Iran, major Muslim states of the wider Middle East, as well as European powers, have clearly expressed their lack of appetite for any such misadventure.
Strong signals are emerging from Tel Aviv and Washington that the US and Israel are planning a new assault on Iran, reportedly after the American midterms on Nov 3 — perhaps even earlier.
The US has been sending more troops and military equipment to the Middle East, and American and Israeli forces have reportedly rehearsed attack plans.

stories.title: Supreme Court questions Sindh govt’s property claim
summary: The observation came as the SC remanded a protracted landlord-tenant dispute to the Sindh High Court (SHC) for fresh adjudication within six months, setting aside its Dec 5, 2023, judgement.
After purchasing the property, Ms Begum served a notice under Section 18 of the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 (SRPO), informing the Sindh government of the change in ownership.

stories.title: Wapda inks Rs133bn deal for Diamer-Bhasha Dam project
summary: LAHORE: The Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) signed an agreement on Saturday with the Power China-IKAN Joint Venture for the Rs133.18 billion hydro-mechanical (HM-1) contract for the Diamer-Bhasha Dam project.

According to a Wapda spokesperson, the agreement was signed at Wapda House by Diamer-Bhasha Dam Project Chief Engineer and Project Director Arif Ali on behalf of the authority and Ling Jianke, the authorised representative of the joint venture.
The spokesperson said the Diamer-Bhasha Dam was a priority project of the federal government for ensuring the country’s water, food and energy security.

stories.title: US Justice Dept demands California counties help identify suspected noncitizen voters
summary: On October 16, the Justice Department warned Los Angeles County and California election officials they could be liable as abettors of a federal crime if they count mail ballots returned by more than 20,000 people the Trump administration says are probably noncitizens.
On Saturday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the Justice Department acted at Trump's direction.

California officials have rejected the Justice Department's demand to set aside those ballots, saying the federal government has not provided sufficient information about how it identified the alleged noncitizens.

stories.title: JUI-F KP directs leaders to quit ARDC
summary: PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakh­tunkhwa chapter of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) on Saturday direc­ted party members appointed to the newly established Area Represen­tative and Development Council (ARDC) to resign within three days.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the party’s provincial general council held at Mufti Mahmood Markaz under the chairmanship of JUI-F KP emir Senator Maulana Attaur Rehman.
JUI-F KP spokesperson Haji Abdul Jalil Jan told Dawn four party members, two each from the merged and settled districts, had been appointed to the council.
